agree.reason: The letter makes three small, low-cost requests in a calm tone and points out that two-thirds of households signed, so a manager who thinks things are handled well has an easy, face-saving reason to reply rather than dismiss it.

honest.reason: Most claims stay within the facts, but 'Five months later' is a time span the brief never gives, and 'more than one day in every eight' is only true if 'this year' ends around mid-November, which the brief doesn't establish.

works_the_facts.reason: It correctly turns 74 of 112 into 'about two-thirds' and the outages into a rate, but it misses the sharpest point the facts allow: a part promised in June within 6 to 8 weeks should have arrived before the 12-day August outage.

right_comparison.reason: It suggests the alternative is more outages with no plan, but it doesn't spell out what happens if nothing changes, such as a repeat of August for the 23 residents over 75 while the part stays 'on order'.

qualification.reason: The deadline is a '[date]' placeholder and the only stated consequence is posting the reply in the lobby, so nothing checkable happens if management misses the deadline, and the planned TV contact is never mentioned.

objections.reason: It answers the passing certificate ('safe when it runs' is not the same as 'keeps running') and the 'few loud people' view (two-thirds of households), and it doesn't invent objections the facts already settle.

fit.reason: It is a properly addressed open letter of roughly 400 words, signed by the secretary, suitable for the lobby, though it isn't framed at all for the TV station audience.
